Rashi on Niddah 33a:10:1.hebrew: אבל אדם ובגדים - או אדם אם תגע בו, או בגדים אם תגע בהם:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:10:1.english: But a person and garments - Either a person if [the bedding] touches him, or garments if [it] touches them.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:11:1.english: Other items, no - Such as a person and earthenware vessels.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:13:1.hebrew: וכל המשכב - ריבויא הוא, ולאו פרטא:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:13:1.english: And every bed - It is an amplification, and not a detail.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:14:1.hebrew: אימא כהיא - בועלה כמותה, דהא אקשינהו קרא:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:14:1.english: Say [he is] like her - The one who has intercourse with her [is] like her, for the verse compared them.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:14:2.english: As a stringency - That both of them impart impurity to a person to impart impurity to garments.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:14:3.hebrew: אף הוא לא תחלוק בין מגעו למשכבו - ולקולא, ששניהם לא יטמאו. דהא במשכבו פשיטא לן שנתקו הכתוב, הלכך במגעו נמי, שאם נגע באדם לא יטמאנו לטמא בגדים, דהא כתיב ותהי נדתה עליו, דהוקשו הוא והיא בהאי קרא:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:14:3.english: So too, regarding him, do not differentiate between his touch and his bedding - And [this means] leniently: that neither of them shall impart impurity [to a person to impart impurity to garments]. For regarding his bedding, it is obvious to us that Scripture detached it [from severe impurity]; therefore, regarding his touch as well, that if he touches a person, he should not impart impurity to him to impart impurity to garments, as it is written: "And her impurity shall be upon him," for he and she were equated in this verse.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:15:1.english: Upon him - It implies being stringent, and not lenient.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:16:1.english: Is it to say that all of them are men who engage in intercourse with menstruating women - For behold, there are unmarried men [among them].

Rashi on Niddah 33a:17:1.hebrew: אם הן יושבות על כל דם ודם - שהן רואות, בין טמא בין טהור, יושבת עליו ז' ימי נדתה, שהתחיל מנינה משנשתנה מראה דם, ותמנה ז' ימים:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:17:1.english: If they sit for each and every blood - That [whenever] they see [blood], whether impure or pure, she sits for it the seven days of her menstrual impurity, such that her count begins from when the appearance of the blood changed, and she counts seven days.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:17:2.hebrew: תקנה גדולה היא להם - אבל אינן עושות כן, אינן מונות אלא מראיה ראשונה כשאר נשים. וזהו קלקולה: שרואה דם אדום ומשלימתו לדם ירוק. כגון, ראתה ירוק תחלה — סבורה היא שהיא טמאה ומונה ממנו ז' ימים, וכשרואה בחמישי שלה דם אדום, אינה משמרת אלא שני ימים להשלים ז' לראייתה הראשונה, והיא צריכה למנות מראייה שניה:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:17:2.english: It is a great remedy for them - But they do not do so; they count only from the first sighting, like other women. And this is her pitfall: that she sees red blood and completes it to [the count of] the green blood. For example, [if] she saw green [blood] first, she believes that she is impure and counts seven days from it, and when she sees red blood on her fifth day, she observes only two days to complete seven for her first sighting, whereas she [actually] needs to count from the second sighting.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:19:1.hebrew: יום שפוסקת בו - כשהיא רואה ג' רצופים לאחר ז' ימי הנדה והויא זבה, ופוסקת באמצע היום, סופרת אותו קצת היום שעד הערב למנין שבעה נקיים, ואנן ז' נקיים שלמים בעינן לזבה:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:19:1.english: The day on which she ceases - When she sees [blood on] three consecutive [days] after the seven days of niddah, and becomes a zava, and ceases [bleeding] in the middle of the day, she counts that part of the day until the evening toward the count of seven clean [days], whereas we require seven complete clean [days] for a zava.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:1:1.english: If we say beneath the zav - Which is the midras of the zav.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:21:1.hebrew: א"כ - דלענין נקיים מקצת היום ככולו: זב שפסק והתחיל לספור וראה קרי, וקיי"ל דסותר אותו היום ותו לא בהמפלת בשמעתא קמייתא (לעיל נדה דף כב.). ואי מקצת היום ככולו, מאי סותר? הא איכא קצת היום לבא:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:21:1.english: If so - That with regard to [the seven] clean [days, we say that] part of the day is like the whole of it: [Take the case of] a zav who ceased [discharging] and began to count, and experienced a seminal emission; and we maintain that it negates that day and no more, in [the chapter] HaMapelet, in the first sugya (above, Niddah 22a). And if part of the day is like the whole of it, what does it negate? Behold, there is [still] part of the day yet to come!

Rashi on Niddah 33a:22:1.english: If she saw in the middle of the day, etc. - It is an objection. And [the Gemara] answers: "And let the verse say to him, etc.," in astonishment.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:23:1.hebrew: וקא מהדר לאוקמי אתקפתיה אין על כרחיך שבקיה לקרא כו' - דכיון דקיי"ל בכל דוכתי מקצת היום ככולו, איהו דחיק ומוקים אנפשיה בסמוך לשקיעת החמה:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:23:1.english: And he seeks to uphold his objection: "Yes, perforce leave the verse, etc." - For since we maintain everywhere that part of the day is like the whole of it, it [the verse] constrains itself and establishes itself [as referring to a case] adjacent to sunset.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:24:1.hebrew: פולטת - כגון ששמשה בזוב, ופסקה, והתחילה למנות, ופלטה — מהו שתסתור מניינה? הא דקי"ל דפולטת טמאה — משום רואה היא, וסתרה:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:24:1.english: A woman who discharges [semen] - For example, where she engaged in intercourse during [her period of] zov, and [her discharge] ceased, and she began to count [her seven clean days], and [then] discharged [semen] — what is [the halakha as to] whether she negates her count? [As for] that which we establish that a woman who discharges [semen] is ritually impure: is it because she is [considered] one who sees [semen], and [therefore] she negates [her count]?

Rashi on Niddah 33a:3:1.hebrew: נתקו הכתוב מטומאה חמורה - מדכתיב: וכל הנוגע בכל אשר יהיה תחתיו יטמא והנושא אותם יכבס בגדיו, ומדלא ערבינהו ונכתוב: וכל הנוגע בכל אשר יהיה תחתיו והנושא אותם יכבס בגדיו, ואפסקינהו ביטמא — מכלל דהאי יטמא לאו באדם ובגדים קמיירי, אלא באוכלין ומשקין. והנושא אותם נדרש בתורת כהנים לנושא משכבו ומושבו של זב:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:3:1.english: The verse removed it from severe impurity - Since it is written: "And whoever touches anything that was under him shall be impure, and he who carries them shall wash his clothes," and since [Scripture] did not combine them and write: "And whoever touches anything that was under him and he who carries them shall wash his clothes," and [instead] separated them with "shall be impure" — it follows that this "shall be impure" does not deal with a person and garments, but rather with food and drink. And "and he who carries them" is expounded in Torat Kohanim as referring to one who carries the bedding and seating of a zav.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:4:1.hebrew: אימא - להכי אפסקינהו קרא, דלא יטמא אדם לטמא בגדים שעליו. להכי כתב יטמא, דאדם לחודיה טמא, או אם נגעו בגדים, יהו בגדים טמאים ולא הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:4:1.english: Say - It was for this reason that the verse separated them: so that it does not impart impurity to a person to impart impurity to garments upon him. [And] for this reason it wrote "shall be impure": that the person alone is impure, or if garments touched [it], the garments shall be impure and not he.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:6:1.hebrew: יעלה לרגלה - יעלה לסופה, כגון בא עליה בששי שלה, יטבול בליל המחרת כמותה:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:6:1.english: He shall count toward her conclusion - He shall count toward her end. For example, if he had intercourse with her on her sixth [day], he would immerse on the night of the following day, just like her.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:6:2.english: Seven days - And even if he engaged in intercourse with her on the seventh [day].

Rashi on Niddah 33a:7:1.hebrew: מה היא מטמאה אדם - לטמא בגדים שעליו, דאתי בקל וחומר ממשכבה, אף הוא מטמא אדם לטמא בגדים שעליו:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:7:1.english: Just as she imparts impurity to a person - To impart impurity to the garments upon him, which is derived via an a fortiori argument from her bedding; so too, he imparts impurity to a person to impart impurity to the garments upon him.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:7:2.hebrew: וכלי חרס - בהיסט. ואע"ג דאין כלי חרס מקבל טומאה אלא מאוירו, בהיסט זב וזבה מיטמא, כדכתיב (ויקרא טו) (כל כלי) חרס אשר יגע בו הזב, ואמרי' במכילתין: איזהו מגעו שהוא ככולו? הוי אומר: זה היסטו:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:7:2.english: And an earthenware vessel - Through shifting. And even though an earthenware vessel does not contract impurity except through its airspace, through the shifting of a zav and a zavah it becomes impure, as it is written (Leviticus 15): “(Every vessel of) earthenware that the zav touches,” and we say in our tractate: What is its touch that is like [contact with] all of it? You must say: This is its shifting.

Rashi on Niddah 33a:9:1.hebrew: שאין ת"ל וכל המשכב אשר ישכב עליו יטמא - שהרי כבר נאמר ותהי נדתה עליו, ובדידה כתיב וכל הנוגע במשכבה יכבס בגדיו:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:9:1.english: For there is no need for the verse to state: "And every bed upon which he lies shall be impure" - For it has already been stated: "And her impurity be upon him," and regarding her it is written: "And whoever touches her bed shall wash his clothes."

Rashi on Niddah 33a:9:2.hebrew: מטומאה חמורה - שלא יהיה משכבו חמור כמשכבה, לטמא אדם ובגדים שעליו:
Rashi on Niddah 33a:9:2.english: From severe impurity - That his bedding should not be as severe as her bedding, to impart impurity to a person and the garments upon him.

Tosafot on Niddah 33a:12:1.english: A generalization and a detail that are distant from one another - [This is] explained in chapter HaChovel (Bava Kamma 85a).

Tosafot on Niddah 33a:17:1.hebrew: תניא א"ר מאיר וכו' - לרבי יוחנן, דאמר בפ' כל היד (לעיל נדה יט:) ירד ר"מ לשיטת עקביא בן מהללאל וטימא דם ירוק, יפרש: דם ירוק דהכא לאו ירוק ממש כי ההיא דלעיל, אלא דיהה ממנו; וכן לעקביא, מטמאה כותית דם ירוק דיהה מדם ירוק שהוא טמא. ולעיל פי' בע"א:
Tosafot on Niddah 33a:17:1.english: It was taught [in a baraita]: Rabbi Meir said, etc. - According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said in the chapter "Kol HaYad" (above, Niddah 19b) that Rabbi Meir accepted the opinion of Akavya ben Mahalalel and deemed green blood impure, he would explain that "green blood" here is not actual green [blood] like that [mentioned] above, but rather paler than it; and similarly according to Akavya, a Samaritan woman is rendered impure on account of green blood that is paler than the green blood that is impure. And above, it was explained in another way.

Tosafot on Niddah 33a:19:1.hebrew: סופרתו למנין ז' - וא"ת: ודאמר בכיצד צולין [ובמס' נזיר] (דף טו:) מקצת היום ככולו, וזבה גדולה אמר התם דמשכחת אליביה ברואה בין השמשות — וכי ככותים סובר? דהכי פריך לקמן (נדה דף סט.) לרב דאמר יום שפוסקת בו עולה למנין שבעה: ורב ככותאי אמרה לשמעתיה? וי"ל: דר' יוסי לית ליה מקצת היום ככולו אלא בסוף ספירה, כמו שומרת יום; אבל בתחלה, כמו שאומרים כותים, מודה דלא אמרינן. ומה שקשה מפ"ק דר"ה (דף י.), נפרש בסוף מכילתין בע"ה:
Tosafot on Niddah 33a:19:1.english: She counts it toward the count of seven - And if you say: But as for that which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin [and in tractate Nazir] (15b), that [according to Rabbi Yosi] part of the day is like the whole of it, and [regarding] a major zava (zava gedola), [the Gemara] says there that [such a case] can be found according to his view [only] when she sees [blood] at twilight — does he then hold like the Cutheans? For this is what [the Gemara] objects later on (Niddah 69a) against Rav, who said: "The day on which she ceases [emitting blood] counts toward the count of seven [clean days]" — "Did Rav state his teaching in accordance with the Cutheans?!" And it can be answered that Rabbi Yosi maintains [that] part of the day is like the whole of it only at the end of a counting, like a woman who watches day for day (shomeret yom); but at the beginning [of the count], as the Cutheans say, he agrees that we do not say [this]. And that which is difficult from the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (10a), we shall explain at the end of our tractate, with the help of God.

Tosafot on Niddah 33a:23:1.hebrew: דאיהו דחיק ומוקי אנפשיה - אין האמת כן, מדפריך בפ' בתרא (לקמן נדה דף סט.): ורב ככותאי אמרה לשמעתיה:
Tosafot on Niddah 33a:23:1.english: For he strains to establish himself - This is not the truth, since [the Gemara] challenges in the last chapter (below, Niddah 69a): "And did Rav say his teaching in accordance with the Cutheans?"

Tosafot on Niddah 33a:24:1.hebrew: רואה הויא וסתרה - אור"י, דמשכחת בשמשה בהיתר שתסתור ע"י פליטה אחר ראיית ג' ימים רצופין, דקי"ל כרבנן בפ' ר' עקיבא (שבת פו:) דבעינן שש עונות שלמות. א"נ, אחר ראייה אחת, ואחר תיקון רבי זירא, דסופרת שבעה נקיים על טיפת דם כחרדל, דמסתמא צריך נמי נקיים מזרע, דכעין דאורייתא תקון. ומכאן, אשה ששמשה וראתה מיד, אין לה להתחיל לספור נקיים עד אחר יום ד', דבעינן ו' עונות שלמות; וכן פסק ר"ח. ואפילו רבא, דפליג הכא ארמי בר חמא, נראה דחזר בו, מדלא השיבו; וכולהו אמוראי סברי פרק יוצא דופן (לקמן נדה דף מב.) דרואה הויא וסתרה, אף לר"ש, וכ"ש לרבנן. והא דקאמר רבא לקמן (נדה דף לז.) ואחר תטהר שלא תהא טומאה מפסקת ביניהם, אביי אומר שלא תהא זיבה מפסקת ביניהם — משם אין להוכיח דרבא לא חזר בו; דהתם איירי בטומאת לידה, שטמאה ז' ועושה משכב ומושב כמו נדה, ולכך קאמר שלא תהא מפסקת; אבל קרי, דלא סותר אלא יום א', לא מפסיק:
Tosafot on Niddah 33a:24:1.english: She is [considered] one who experienced an emission and negates - Ri says that you can find [a case] where she engaged in relations in a permitted manner and would negate [a day] through a discharge [of semen] after seeing [blood for] three consecutive days, for we establish in accordance with the Rabbis in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Akiva" (Shabbat 86b) that we require six complete periods (onot) [for semen to lose its viability]. Alternatively, [this can occur] after a single sighting [of blood], and [this is] after the enactment of Rabbi Zeira that [a woman] counts seven clean days [even] for a drop of blood [as small as] a mustard seed; for presumably, [these seven days] must also be clean from semen, as they enacted [rabbinic measures] modeled after biblical law. And from here [it is derived that] a woman who engaged in relations and immediately saw [blood] must not begin to count clean [days] until after the fourth day, for we require six complete onot; and so ruled Rabbeinu Ḥananel (R"Ch). And even Rava, who disagrees here with Rami bar Ḥama, it appears that he retracted, since he did not reply to him [i.e., to the Gemara's objection]. And all the Amoraim maintain in the chapter [entitled] "Yotzei Dofan" (below, Niddah 42a) that she is [considered] one who experienced an emission and negates [a day], even according to Rabbi Shimon, and all the more so according to the Rabbis. And as for that which Rava says below (Niddah 37a): "And after that she shall be pure" — that there should be no impurity separating between them, [whereas] Abaye says: that there should be no zivah separating between them — from there, there is no proof that Rava did not retract. For there, it is dealing with the impurity of childbirth, which is impure for seven [days] and imparts impurity to items used for lying and sitting (mishkav u-moshav) like a menstruating woman (niddah), and therefore he said that it must not separate; but a seminal emission (keri), which negates only one day, does not separate.

Tosafot on Niddah 33a:2:1.hebrew: והנשא כתיב - חסר וי"ו. תימה, דבמסורת הוא מלא; מיהו, מצינו שהמסורת הוא חולק על הש"ס במסכת שבת (דף נה:), גבי בני עלי: מעבירם כתיב, ובמקראות שלנו כתיב מעבירים מלא:
Tosafot on Niddah 33a:2:1.english: "Ve-hanisa" is written - [That is, it is written] lacking a vav. [This is] puzzling, for in the Masorah it is [spelled] plene [with a vav]; however, we find that the Masorah disagrees with the Talmud in Tractate Shabbat (folio 55b) regarding the sons of Eli, [where the Gemara states] that it is written "ma'aviram" [defective], whereas in our scriptures it is written "ma'avirim," plene.

Tosafot on Niddah 33a:7:1.hebrew: מה היא מטמאה אדם וכלי חרס - משום דבהשותפין (ב"ב ט:) גבי נושא נבלה ומדרס, אע"ג דמטמא שאר בגדים שעליו, אינו מטמא אדם וכלי חרס; לכך נקטינהו הכא:
Tosafot on Niddah 33a:7:1.english: Just as she imparts impurity to a person and earthenware vessels - Because in [chapter] HaShuttafin (Bava Batra 9b), regarding one who carries a carcass and [one who carries] a midras, even though he imparts impurity to the other garments upon him, he does not impart impurity to a person or earthenware vessels; therefore, [the Tanna] specified these here.
